location: ADR-010 Web2App return; ADR-009 polling; Flow state machine (Poll OK row)
trigger_condition: Web2App callback opens in a new tab and 'the cookie and callback value are invalidated on first use', while the original tab polls local status using that same cookie. The document never says which response delivers the authorization-code redirect.
potential_consequence: Two implementers differ: code delivered to the callback tab, to the polling tab (which no longer has a cookie), to both, or to neither. A verified user is stranded, or the code is handed to the wrong browser context. The binding guarantee cannot be proven.
guard_snippet: Normative rule: in Web2App flows only the callback response may emit the redirect (303 with code and iss) and clear the cookie; the polling tab only renders 'continue in the other tab' and never receives a code. Test: two tabs, callback tab gets the code once, polling tab gets none.

location: ADR-003 Certificate verification; Source reconciliation (Q-02); Flow state machine
trigger_condition: Revocation (OCSP via AIA, CRL fallback; facts note section 4 step 4) is required but the doc leaves who performs it to Q-02. There is no timeout, no hard-fail versus soft-fail rule, no state-machine row for 'status unavailable', and AIA/CRL URLs come from the certificate.
potential_consequence: Implementers choose fail-open (a revoked certificate logs in) or fail-closed, and each one is arguably compliant. Cert-supplied URLs are an SSRF/egress channel that contradicts the egress-isolation claim. Revocation latency inside the poll path eats the retry budget.
guard_snippet: Rule: revocation status unknown, stale or unreachable => failed(verification_failed, reason=status_unavailable), never verified. Fetch only over HTTP(S) to the allow-listed responder hosts in config, with a hard timeout (e.g. 5s) and no redirects. Add a status_unavailable row to the state table and a no-egress-to-unlisted-host test.

location: ADR-009 Polling vs Capacity model (pending-flow cap 10,000; upstream concurrency)
trigger_condition: Admission is capped at 10,000 pending flows. Upstream concurrency is a separate semaphore with 'no default without Q-01'. Each flow holds one long poll of up to 60,500 ms, and the text also says 'one server-side poller'.
potential_consequence: With 10,000 admitted flows and a small semaphore, most flows never get a poll slot before the flow timeout. A user approves on the phone and the bridge reports 'expired'. 'One poller' and 'one long poll per flow' contradict each other, so implementations diverge.
guard_snippet: Admit a flow only if a poll slot is reservable: pending_cap = min(NFR-003 default, upstream_concurrency). Define the poller as N workers sharing the semaphore, each long poll using timeoutMs <= (flow_timeout / 2) with round-robin fairness. Test: more flows than slots still completes every admitted flow.

location: ADR-009 Overflow; Capacity model (per-client bucket); Threat table 'Push spam'
trigger_condition: The authorize endpoint is unauthenticated and client_id is public. The per-client token bucket is shared by all users. 'Pending and verified are never evicted' is silent on whether 'created' entries are evictable (E04 says nothing is evicted).
potential_consequence: One attacker draining a victim client's bucket, or filling the store with 10,000 'created' flows (about 167/s for 60s), makes every legitimate login for that client return 503. A per-IP bucket is defeated by IPv6 or proxy-collapsed IPs.
guard_snippet: Charge the per-client bucket only after redirect_uri validation. Add a per-IP cap on 'created' flows. State: 'created' entries are the only evictable class, oldest first, before any 503. Test: flood from one IP leaves a second IP and a second client unaffected.

location: Flow state machine (rows 'Web2App callback without cookie', 'callback fails checks'); ADR-010; paragraph under the table
trigger_condition: The callback row says cookie-less is 'pending: stay'. ADR-010 says the callback 'fails'. The text says 'shows the restart page and leaves the flow to expire'. No row covers a valid callback arriving while the poll is still RUNNING (the facts note says polling and callback order is free).
potential_consequence: If a callback that beats the poll is treated as failing the checks (it cannot compare userChallenge yet), a legitimate user lands in 'failed'. A cookie-bearing callback with a bad value kills a flow that a late, correct callback could finish.
guard_snippet: Add rows: callback valid but poll RUNNING => pending, record callback_seen, finish on the next COMPLETE/OK. Callback with cookie but bad value => failed. Callback without cookie => restart page, state unchanged (and say so in ADR-010 instead of 'fails').

location: ADR-008 Access token and userinfo
trigger_condition: AEAD uses client_id as associated data, but userinfo receives only an opaque bearer token with no client authentication. The token's plaintext layout (token family ID, exp, scope, claims, K_at version, AEAD nonce) and where client_id/kid sit are unspecified.
potential_consequence: Implementations cannot interoperate or be proven safe. Either client_id travels in clear in the token (the 'opaque' claim is violated and the AAD check is circular), or decrypt is tried per client. The allow-list for personal_code could be evaluated at issue time or at use time, with different results after a config change.
guard_snippet: Specify: token = version(1) || kid(1) || nonce(12) || ct||tag, AAD = 'eidbridge-at-v1'||0x00||client_id, with client_id stored inside the plaintext and re-compared to AAD after decrypt. Plaintext = {fid, exp, scope, claims}. Evaluate the personal_code allow-list at userinfo time.

location: ADR-007 `sub` rule; ADR-003 Certificate verification step on identity
trigger_condition: The HMAC input uses 'country' and 'code', but the source is the certificate Subject serialNumber (e.g. PNOEE-30001010004, facts note section 4 step 8). The semantics-identifier type (PNO, PAS, IDC), prefix parsing, case and whitespace normalization are unspecified.
potential_consequence: Two builds produce different subs for the same person, or a PAS/IDC identifier and a PNO code with the same digits collide into one sub (account takeover at the client). Rotation and migration tests cannot be fixture-compared.
guard_snippet: Define: parse serialNumber with ^(PNO|PAS|IDC)([A-Z]{2})-(.+)$, reject any other form, and set HMAC input = 'eidbridge-sub-v1'||0x00||sector||0x00||type||0x00||country||0x00||code, with code verbatim (no case folding). Add published test vectors.

location: Configuration invariants (rows 'Production key whose SPKI is in the demo keystore', 'Demo mode with production host/RP UUID', 'No trusted proxy ... every peer address is private')
trigger_condition: The invariants need data the process does not have. Demo keys are auto-generated per deployment, so a production host has no demo keystore. Production RP UUIDs are operator-specific and cannot be recognised. Peer addresses and load-balancer status are unknown at startup.
potential_consequence: The checks are either no-ops or untestable (E16, E18, A12). A demo-generated key copied to production passes. The proxy-trust 'warning' can never fire, and per-IP limiting collapses to the proxy address (all users share one bucket) with no signal.
guard_snippet: Rewrite as checkable rules: demo mode accepts only the published demo RP UUID/host/CA allow-list, and production rejects keys carrying kid prefix 'demo-' or flagged by a persisted marker. Replace the proxy rule with a startup-time config check: trusted_proxies is required whenever bind address is not loopback, else fail.

location: Threat table 'Push spam, enumeration'; Flow state machine; facts note section 1b/API-DETAILS
trigger_condition: Notification mode takes a user-entered national code. Limits are per IP and per client only. Terminal outcomes (failed/init error, refused, expired) are distinct. The pinned docs say RPs should not show different messages per error cause, to hinder enumeration.
potential_consequence: A distributed attacker pushes spam to one victim indefinitely. Differences in init-error and refusal pages or timing reveal whether a national code has a Smart-ID account.
guard_snippet: Add a per-target-identity bucket (HMAC of the identifier, not stored in plain) e.g. N pushes per window across all IPs/clients. Rule: init error, 404, ACCOUNT_UNUSABLE and DOCUMENT_UNUSABLE render the same generic page with constant-time behaviour. Test with two identities.

location: Capacity model (Tombstone cap, Code store cap); Data lifecycle (Code tombstone)
trigger_condition: One code slot is reserved per flow at creation, but the tombstone is created at code exchange with no reservation. 'Full means 503 at flow creation' cannot protect an exchange that happens later. It is also unspecified what happens when tombstone or deny-list storage is full at exchange.
potential_consequence: At exchange, either a verified user is refused (code consumed, no tokens) or the tombstone is skipped, which silently disables replay detection. This contradicts 'replay detection never degrades'.
guard_snippet: Make the slot convertible: the reserved code slot becomes the tombstone slot at exchange (total cap = codes + tombstones, reserved at flow creation). Deny-list full => reject the newest replay-family userinfo calls fail-closed. Test: store at cap, exchange succeeds and replay is still detected.

location: ADR-010 Web2App return; ADR-003 'a returned flowType the bridge offered'; ADR-009 'Upstream session created when the QR page loads'
trigger_condition: initialCallbackUrl is part of the session-creation request and of the signed payload; it must be empty for QR (facts note 3e). One session is created at QR page load, but the doc offers QR and Web2App from that page without saying how the callback URL is chosen or what 'offered' flowTypes are recorded.
potential_consequence: A session created with a callback cannot be shown as a QR, or one created without cannot do Web2App. Implementers pick UA sniffing, two sessions (doubling quota use and push spam), or a mismatch that fails signature verification for every user.
guard_snippet: Specify: flow type is decided before session creation (explicit user choice or UA-based on the page request) and stored as flow.offered = {QR} or {Web2App}; initialCallbackUrl empty iff QR. Verification accepts signature.flowType only if it is in flow.offered.

location: ADR-010 Flow cookie ('one per flow, named __Host-eidb-<flow-id>')
trigger_condition: Any web page can send the victim's browser to the authorize endpoint (all inputs are attacker-chosen but valid), and each request sets a new flow cookie. There is no cap on cookies per browser or cleanup of abandoned cookies, and every request must scan them.
potential_consequence: A cookie bomb pushes the Cookie header over server or proxy limits (431/400) for the whole origin, a login DoS on that browser. Cookie jar limits evict the cookie of a genuine in-progress flow.
guard_snippet: Cap at K live flow cookies per browser (e.g. 4): on creating the K+1th, overwrite the oldest via Set-Cookie expiry. Look up the cookie by the flow handle in the URL only. Test: 50 authorize requests leave a header under 4 KB.

location: ADR-008 Authorization code ('Any failed exchange still consumes it'); Data lifecycle tombstone
trigger_condition: A failed exchange (wrong PKCE, failed client authentication or redirect_uri) consumes the code, but the tombstone maps code hash to a token family, and no family exists for a failed exchange. The cited RFC 6749 4.1.2 requires denial of reuse and does not mandate consumption on failure.
potential_consequence: A later legitimate exchange of that code is treated as a replay and adds a phantom family to the deny-list. A party that merely holds the code (for example from a log) can burn it before the real client exchanges it. The behaviour is undefined for the failed-then-valid sequence.
guard_snippet: Specify: any presented code is LoadAndDelete'd; on failure write a tombstone with family=none, and a later presentation returns invalid_grant without deny-listing anything. Test the sequences wrong-then-correct and correct-then-wrong.

location: ADR-007 Procedure table and Key persistence
trigger_condition: K_sub is stored with the signing key and is the sole defence against enumeration of guessable national codes, yet only signing-key and K_at compromise have procedures. The emergency steps remove the key from JWKS and never say that a replacement signing key is generated and activated.
potential_consequence: After a K_sub leak every sub is reversible by brute force over national codes and the doc offers no response. After an emergency revocation of the only signing key the provider cannot issue ID tokens (outage) or implementers improvise.
guard_snippet: Add a K_sub-compromise procedure (new K_sub version, migration window with previous_sub, immediate retirement of the old version and notification of clients). Add to Emergency revocation: 'generate and activate a new signing key before removal, publish its kid in JWKS'. Drill both.

location: ADR-009 SIGTERM; ADR-002 lifecycle
trigger_condition: SIGTERM drains 'until the 60-second code TTL or grace period', but pending flows live up to flow timeout + 30s and a code issued at second 59 lives until second 119.
potential_consequence: Users who approved on their phone are dropped at second 60, and codes issued during the drain are lost when the process exits before exchange. The behaviour at the drain boundary is undefined.
guard_snippet: Define drain end = max(longest remaining pending flow, newest issued code expiry) bounded by the grace period, and 503 new QR page loads during drain. Test: flow verified at T+55 still exchanges.

location: Flow state machine (missing inputs); ADR-009 'Upstream session'
trigger_condition: The table has no input for: a reload or second request of the QR page on a 'pending' flow (listed as 'discard', so what is rendered?), the upstream concurrency semaphore being saturated when the page loads, and how 'browser abandon' is detected (no signal exists), or whether explicit cancel needs POST plus cookie.
potential_consequence: A refresh creates a second upstream session (quota and push spam) or shows a blank page. A flow stuck in 'created' waits for the 60s TTL. A cancel reachable by cross-site GET lets any site cancel a victim's flow (Lax cookies are sent on top-level GETs).
guard_snippet: Add rows: 'QR page re-request, pending' => re-render from stored state, no new session; 'semaphore full at page load' => created stays, render 'busy, retry' with 503 and Retry-After; abandon only by timeout; cancel is POST with CSRF binding token. Add tests.

location: ADR-009 Per-IP bucket; Configuration invariants (proxy row)
trigger_condition: The rate-limit key is 'the resolved client IP'. The key for IPv6 (per /128 vs /64), for private peers behind an untrusted proxy, and the behaviour when X-Forwarded-For has many entries are unspecified. The unsafe default is 'start with a warning'.
potential_consequence: An attacker with an IPv6 /64 gets effectively unlimited buckets. Behind a proxy all users share one bucket (self-DoS) or all share the attacker's. Spoofed hops are mis-resolved.
guard_snippet: Key = IPv4 /32 or IPv6 /64. Resolve by taking the rightmost non-trusted hop from the configured trusted_proxies and refuse to start in production without trusted_proxies unless direct_internet=true is set explicitly.

location: ADR-008 Configuration row; ADR-009; ADR-002 (flow timeout, flow TTL, retry budget, clock skew)
trigger_condition: 'Flow timeout', 'flow TTL' (cookie Max-Age), retry budget and backoff, clock skew, body and header limits, rate thresholds and Retry-After are named but have no values, no bounds and no startup rule. 'Flow timeout' and 'flow TTL' are used for what seems to be the same quantity.
potential_consequence: Two builds behave differently, and several tests (E03, E04, E19) cannot be written. A very large flow timeout inflates every cap, while one under the upstream TIMEOUT breaks every login. There is no unsafe-default guard.
guard_snippet: Require each value at startup (fail if unset) within stated bounds, e.g. flow_timeout in [60s,300s] and >= upstream timeoutMs + margin; one name (flow_ttl) used for cookie Max-Age, flow timeout and the 30s grace; retry_budget = N attempts within M seconds with exponential backoff.

location: ADR-008 Endpoints ('GET authorize, GET userinfo'); ADR-005 OIDF Basic OP plan
trigger_condition: OIDC Core requires the Authorization Endpoint and the UserInfo Endpoint to support both GET and POST (sections 3.1.2.1 and 5.3.1). The doc lists GET only and also commits to the OIDF Basic OP plan. 'Tokens in URLs' is addressed only for userinfo.
potential_consequence: The conformance run fails and RPs that POST (large requests, userinfo POST) break. If POST is added ad hoc, the CSRF and body-size rules differ from GET.
guard_snippet: Either list 'authorize: GET and POST; userinfo: GET and POST (bearer in header only)' with identical validation, or record a deviation row with the plan modules that are expected to fail.

location: ADR-008 userinfo and ID token; ADR-004 evaluation; facts note section 4 ('Other Subject attributes: NOT FOUND')
trigger_condition: The claim set is never defined. There is no scope-to-claim mapping, no rule for a missing or absent openid scope, and no statement of what the certificate supplies (name attributes are not verified in the pinned facts). The 'claims' parameter is excluded, so there is no other way to select claims.
potential_consequence: Implementers return different claims (names, email, personal_code) and different data minimisation. Claims not backed by the certificate could be fabricated. personal_code exposure depends on a per-client allow-list with no scope gate.
guard_snippet: Add a table: scope openid => sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, auth_time, nonce, acr, amr; scope profile => given_name, family_name only if present in the verified certificate subject; personal_code => only with the explicit scope and the client allow-list. Missing openid => invalid_scope.

location: ADR-008 Authorization code ('Random'); ADR-010 ('unguessable', 'random binding token'); Data lifecycle
trigger_condition: No minimum entropy, encoding, or hash function is given for authorization codes, flow handles/ids, binding tokens, callback values or token-family IDs.
potential_consequence: 'Unguessable' cannot be tested. A 32-bit handle or non-constant-time compare passes review. Code-hash keys using a fast unsalted hash are fine only at >=128 bits of entropy.
guard_snippet: Require crypto/rand with >=128 bits (256 for codes and binding tokens), base64url, SHA-256 for hashing stored codes, constant-time comparison for all secrets. Test by length and a compare-function lint.

location: ADR-002 Decision and Data lifecycle ('overwritten before release'); E06 TestLateResultDiscardedAndSecretsZeroed
trigger_condition: The rule requires secrets and the plaintext claim set to be overwritten. In Go, strings are immutable and maps, JSON and GC copies cannot be zeroed, and the spec does not require []byte-only handling.
potential_consequence: The rule is unverifiable and the test can only check a field the implementation chose to clear, giving false assurance about PII and sessionSecret in memory.
guard_snippet: Restate as achievable: secrets and certificate bytes are held only in []byte or a wrapper type, cleared with clear() on terminal state; the claim set is not copied into strings beyond the minimum; core dumps disabled; the claim 'zeroed' is limited to those fields and the residual risk disclosed.

location: ADR-003 TLS identity and `TLS_PINS=disabled`; Configuration invariants
trigger_condition: Behaviour for TLS_PINS unset, empty, malformed, containing only 'next', or disabled in demo mode is unspecified. The disable sentinel shares the field with pin values.
potential_consequence: An unset or typo'd value could silently mean 'no pin check' (the unsafe default), or production starts with a pin set that matches nothing and every login fails.
guard_snippet: Table: unset/empty => fail in both modes; unparsable => fail; list must contain at least one 'current' pin; 'disabled' valid only with the acknowledgement flag in production. Move the disable switch to a separate explicit setting (tls_pin_mode=enforce|disabled).

location: ADR-009 Clock; ADR-008 Replay deny-list; Data lifecycle
trigger_condition: Store TTLs (tombstone, deny-list) use the monotonic clock, while access-token exp, sealed inside the token, is wall-clock. After a backwards wall-clock step, tokens stay valid longer than the monotonic deny-list entry.
potential_consequence: A denied token family becomes usable again after its deny-list entry expires although the token's wall-clock exp has not passed.
guard_snippet: Set deny-list/tombstone lifetime = max token lifetime + clock skew measured on the same clock, and reject at userinfo any token whose wall exp exceeds issue-time monotonic exp (store both at seal time). Test with an injected clock step.

location: Configuration invariants (HTTP issuer allowed in demo) vs ADR-010 cookie `__Host-` with `Secure`
trigger_condition: Demo mode permits an HTTP issuer, but the flow cookie requires Secure (the __Host- prefix), which browsers reject on non-secure origins other than localhost.
potential_consequence: Every demo flow served over plain HTTP loses its cookie, so binding checks fail for all users, or implementers drop Secure in demo and diverge from production tests.
guard_snippet: Require HTTPS (or http://localhost only) in demo too, or specify an explicit non-prefixed cookie name for localhost demo that production forbids.

location: ADR-008 Client authentication (private_key_jwt)
trigger_condition: If private_key_jwt ships (Q-03), the accepted aud values, jti replay cache bound, iat/exp limits and alg allow-list are unspecified.
potential_consequence: Accepting several aud values (issuer and endpoint) enables assertion replay across endpoints, and an unbounded jti cache is another memory exhaustion path. Cross-implementation behaviour differs.
guard_snippet: Accept aud == issuer only; require jti, exp within 60s, bounded jti store (count and TTL) with 503 when full; alg limited to RS256/ES256; reject if iss != sub != client_id.
